description: Evolve molecular property prediction models for ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) endpoints critical to drug discovery. Focus on hERG cardiac toxicity, a major cause of drug candidate attrition.

problem.goal: Maximize ROC-AUC for predicting hERG channel inhibition (cardiac toxicity) from molecular structure
constraints: Must use only molecular structure as input (SMILES)
Model must be interpretable or provide feature importance
No data leakage between train/validation/test splits

code_requirements: ALL imports must be at module level (top of file), not inside methods
Use 'from rdkit import Chem' and 'from rdkit.Chem import AllChem, Descriptors' at top
AVOID CalcPBF - it requires 3D conformers which we don't generate
AVOID RDKFingerprint module - use Chem.RDKFingerprint(mol) instead
Handle invalid SMILES gracefully (Chem.MolFromSmiles returns None)
Use numpy arrays, not lists, for feature matrices
Ensure predict_proba returns values in [0, 1] range

optimization_strategies: 3D FEATURES NOW AVAILABLE: Use pre-cached 3D pharmacophore features from data/embeddings/
3D PHARMACOPHORE CRITICAL: N-aromatic distances rank #1-2 in feature importance for hERG
CRITICAL INSIGHT: Compact fingerprints (512 bits) OUTPERFORM larger (1024/2048 bits) on small datasets - reduces noise
CURRENT BEST (gen12c): 512-bit Morgan + MACCS + 25 descriptors, 4-model ensemble achieves 0.890 ROC-AUC
CRITICAL INSIGHT: Extreme regularization (shallow trees depth 3-6, few estimators 80-100) works BEST on this small dataset
Use extended Morgan (radius=3, 1024 bits) + MACCS (167 bits) + 25 molecular descriptors
CRITICAL: The best approach combines Morgan fingerprints (2048 bits) + molecular descriptors in the SAME model
Use hybrid feature concatenation: np.concatenate([morgan_fp_array, descriptor_array])
Include these TOP descriptors: MolLogP, BasicNitrogenCount, NumAromaticRings, TPSA, MolWt
Try dual fingerprints: Morgan (2048) + MACCS keys (167 bits) together
Ensemble 3 diverse classifiers: RF + GBM + (ExtraTrees OR SVM) with weights ~[0.35, 0.35, 0.30]
Scale ONLY the continuous descriptors, NOT the binary fingerprint bits
Count basic nitrogens manually: sp3 N with formal charge >= 0 (key hERG pharmacophore)
Try different fingerprint radii: radius=2 is default, radius=3 captures extended environment
Use class_weight='balanced' for Random Forest and ExtraTrees
GBM handles mixed binary+continuous features well, try learning_rate 0.05-0.1
Feature selection (SelectKBest, k=500-1000) can help reduce noise for smaller models

3d_features_available: Key pharmacophore: N-aromatic distances, aromatic-aromatic distances
Shape: PMI, asphericity, eccentricity, radius of gyration

trust._comment: Trust validation is MANDATORY for this drug discovery project

domain_context.background: hERG (human Ether-a-go-go Related Gene) encodes a potassium ion channel. Drug-induced hERG inhibition causes cardiac arrhythmias (QT prolongation), leading to drug withdrawals. Predicting hERG liability early saves billions in failed drug development.
key_molecular_features: Basic nitrogen (positive charge at physiological pH) - count sp3 N with H
Hydrophobic aromatic groups - NumAromaticRings, aromatic atom count
Lipophilicity - MolLogP (optimal range 2-5 for hERG binding)
